notes: With the Lean rank-7 witness bounds/N-m4-upper-7.json this moves the cell to 6 <= chi(N^4) <= 7. The argument (docs/notes/qutrit_m4_rank5_exclusion.md, sections 2 and 10) depends on: (1) Fact A: every one-qutrit slice of a rank-5 decomposition of |N>^4 has all five terms nonzero, from chi(N^3) = 4, the unique rank-4 decomposition of |N>^3, and the 0 lifts of relaxed_lift.py at R = 5 (declared, not re-run). (2) Fact B of PR #86 (two_qutrit_slice.py, not re-run): no two-qutrit slice point of a rank-5 decomposition has exactly three nonzero terms. (3) The base-point argument (note, section 2): every term is a nine-slice or diagonal-line term along qutrits 1, 2, at most one is a line term, and every diagonal line meets the monomial-symmetry orbit of (0, 0), so one base point per cover suffices. (4) The two-qutrit slice structure lemma of PR #86; the matcher allows every flat through x_0 and does not use Facts A and B. (5) Exactness: amplitudes lie in Q(omega_3); 65521 and 2013265921 are 1 mod 3, so the modular kernels list supersets, and every candidate and hit is re-decided mod 2013265921 and numerically. (6) Stage C reconstructs cancelling copies, refuses unpinned or ambiguous block reconstructions loudly (recorded as undecided), lists the cancel-at-base multisets, and carries a single block's coefficient family as an unknown; the 27 covers with two blocks in one Pauli orbit were decided without a refusal. (7) Controls (note, sections 5 and 7; results/N/control_*.json and results/controls/): cover counts against the stored lists and slice_lift, planted and product decompositions (270 of 270), the rank-4 decomposition of |N>^3 by 2 + 1 slicing, and the rank-7 witness recovered exactly once from base 4. All Python, no compiled kernel. Attested because no certificate budget re-runs the 38 CPU-hours.
